panels.shot: split diagonal composition, half showing warlike alliance, half looming confrontation
panels.action: On one side, Aditya I Chola and Aparajita Pallava stand back-to-back as allies amid a hazy battlefield; on the other, they face each other tensely across the Ariyil river landscape with Kanchi’s towers distant behind.

dialogue.text: Once they shared a battlefield. A few years later, one ended the other—and with him, centuries of Pallava rule over Kanchi.

i18n.hi: कभी दोनों साथ लड़े। कुछ ही सालों में, एक ने दूसरे को मिटा दिया — और उसके साथ कांची पर सदियों की पल्लव हुकूमत खत्म हुई।

panels.shot: wide aerial over Kanchi, early morning light
panels.action: A majestic view of ancient Kanchipuram with its temples, gopuras, and walls, the city ringed by green fields and distant low hills under a pale dawn sky.

dialogue.text: For centuries, Kanchi was Pallava heartland: a stone forest of temples, scholars, and kings guarding the northern gate of Tamil country.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक कांची पल्लवों का किला रहा — पत्थर के मंदिर, विद्वान, राजा… जो तमिल देश के उत्तरी दरवाज़े की रखवाली करते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Aparajita in court, slight low angle
panels.action: Aparajita Pallava sits on a modest but dignified throne in an audience hall, counselors around him, palm-leaf records at his side, his face thoughtful yet wary.

dialogue.text: In the late ninth century, Aparajita Pallava held this ancient city, but his realm was no longer unchallenged. Chalukyas, Pandyas, and Cholas pressed at its edges.

i18n.hi: नौवीं सदी के अंत में अपराजित पल्लव इस पुरानी नगरी पर बैठा था, पर उसका राज अब बेचुनौती नहीं रहा। चालुक्य, पांड्य और चोल किनारों से धकेल रहे थे।

panels.action: A younger Aditya I Chola stands respectfully before Aparajita in a camp tent, both in war attire, their hands clasped as formal allies while a campaign map lies between them.

dialogue.text: To the south, the Cholas were rising again. Their prince, Aditya I, first appears in the record not as a conqueror of Kanchi—but as Aparajita’s ally.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में चोल फिर सिर उठा रहे थे। उनका युवराज आदित्य प्रथम रिकॉर्ड में पहले कांची के विजेता के रूप में नहीं, अपराजित के साथी के रूप में दिखता है।

panels.action: On a dusty battlefield, Aditya and Aparajita ride in the same direction leading their respective contingents, enemy forces retreating in the distance as banners of Pallava and Chola flutter together.

dialogue.text: Together they fought the Pandyas and other rivals in the south. Chola plates remember Aditya as a warrior who helped tilt the balance against shared enemies.

i18n.hi: दोनों ने मिलकर पांड्यों और दूसरे दक्षिणी दुश्मनों से लड़ाइयाँ लड़ीं। चोल ताम्रपट आदित्य को उस वीर के रूप में याद करते हैं जिसने मिलकर बाज़ी पलटी।

panels.shot: close-up on a copper plate inscription being engraved
panels.action: A craftsman carefully engraves a long copper plate, stylus biting into metal as lines of Grantha-Tamil script unfurl; a royal seal rests nearby.

dialogue.text: Yet the only detailed story we have is the Chola version, cut into copper plates a century later. The Pallava voice falls suddenly, eerily silent.

i18n.hi: पर हमारे पास साफ़ कहानी सिर्फ़ चोलों की है, जो सौ साल बाद ताम्रपत्रों पर उकेरी गई। पल्लवों की आवाज़ अचानक, अनजाने में, खामोश हो जाती है।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye over Tondaimandalam, stylized but realistic
panels.action: A stylized but grounded bird’s-eye of Tondaimandalam shows Kanchi, the Ariyil river zone, and the plains stretching south toward the Kaveri delta, with subtle markings hinting at routes and strategic points.

dialogue.text: Between Kanchi and the Kaveri lay Tondaimandalam—the land of the northern Tamils. Whoever held it controlled the road between old Pallava power and the resurging Chola heartland.

i18n.hi: कांची और कावेरी के बीच था तोण्डैमंडलम — उत्तरी तमिलों की धरती। जो इसे पकड़े, वही पुराने पल्लव बल और उभरते चोल दिल के बीच की राह पकड़ता।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Aditya in the Kaveri region, contemplative
panels.action: Aditya stands on a riverbank in the Kaveri country, armor loosened, gazing northward thoughtfully as farmers work in lush fields behind him and a small shrine rises at the edge of the water.

dialogue.text: From the Kaveri delta, Aditya slowly rebuilt Chola strength. Step by careful step, his banners moved north, first as allied arms, then as a power in their own right.

i18n.hi: कावेरी डेल्टा से आदित्य ने धीरे–धीरे चोल ताकत खड़ी की। संभल–संभल कर उसके ध्वज उत्तर बढ़े — पहले साथी की तलवार बनकर, फिर अपनी अलग ताकत।

panels.shot: tense mid-shot in a pavilion, profile view of both
panels.action: In a campaign pavilion, Aditya and Aparajita stand in profile facing each other across a low table with boundary markers and palm-leaf records, their expressions controlled but taut.

dialogue.text: Somewhere in these years, alliance turned to tension. The records do not say why. They only show the result: a Chola king now claiming what Pallava lords once guarded.

i18n.hi: इन सालों में कहीं दोस्ती में खटास घुली। शिलालेख वजह नहीं बताते, बस नतीजा दिखाते हैं — चोल नरेश अब वही ज़मीन माँग रहे हैं जिसे कभी पल्लव सरदार बचाते थे।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Ariyil river zone, late afternoon
panels.action: The Ariyil river winds through a flat Tamil plain dotted with palms and scattered villages; distant dust clouds and faint lines of soldiers hint at an approaching army on each bank.

dialogue.text: The Chola plates speak of the Ariyil river. Near this quiet water, around 897, the old order and the new met with spears and chariots between them.

i18n.hi: चोल ताम्रपट अरियिल नदी का ज़िक्र करते हैं। इसी शांत जल के पास, करीब ८९७ में, पुरानी और नई दुनिया ने भालों और रथों के बीच आमना–सामना किया।

panels.shot: cinematic wide of opposing battle lines before clash
panels.action: Two armies face each other across uneven ground by the river, Pallava standards with the lion emblem opposite Chola tiger banners; Aparajita and Aditya are visible at their respective centers.

dialogue.text: We do not know the numbers, nor every move. We know only this: Aparajita Pallava stood in the field as king, and Aditya Chola faced him as rival.

i18n.hi: ना हमें फौजें पता, ना हर चाल। बस इतना दिखता है — अपराजित पल्लव मैदान में राजा बन खड़ा था, और आदित्य चोल उसके सामने प्रतिद्वंदी।

panels.shot: medium shot on Aditya amid the melee, dynamic but non-graphic
panels.action: Amid swirling dust and the press of armored warriors, Aditya rides forward with controlled intensity, arm outstretched in command, as his troops surge ahead; the river glints in the background.

dialogue.text: Later Chola grants remember Aditya as the king who ‘felled Aparajita in battle.’ Their words are spare, but the weight of the claim is immense.

i18n.hi: बाद के चोल दान आदित्य को उस राजा के रूप में याद करते हैं जिसने ‘अपराजित को रण में गिराया’। शब्द कम हैं, दावा भारी।

panels.shot: mid-wide on collapsing Pallava line, focus on Aparajita’s figure
panels.action: The Pallava line wavers; Aparajita, still upright on his elephant, appears surrounded by confusion as some of his men fall away, the sky hazed with smoke and dust.

dialogue.text: No Pallava plate answers how their ruler fell. No poet of Kanchi records his last command. After Ariyil, the Pallava chronicle simply stops.

i18n.hi: कोई पल्लव ताम्रपट नहीं बताता कि उनका राजा कैसे ढह गया। कांची का कोई कवि उसकी आख़िरी आज्ञा नहीं लिखता। अरियिल के बाद पल्लव गाथा यकबयक थम जाती है।

panels.shot: somber close-up of Aditya after the battle, dusk light
panels.action: As the sun sinks, Aditya stands quiet at the edge of the battlefield, armor dusty, gaze distant; behind him soldiers gather abandoned standards and tend to tired animals.

dialogue.text: “The land remembers the victor,” he says softly. “But the battle remembers all.”

i18n.hi: “ज़मीन विजेता को याद रखती है,” वह धीमे कहता है। “पर लड़ाई सबको याद रखती है।”

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle of Aditya entering Kanchi
panels.action: Aditya rides into Kanchi through a stone gateway, Chola tiger banners rising above the walls while temple towers loom beyond; townspeople watch cautiously from the sides of the street.

dialogue.text: With Aparajita gone, Kanchi bowed to the Cholas. The Leiden grant later speaks, with pride, of Tondaimandalam now under their seal.

i18n.hi: अपराजित के जाते ही कांची ने चोलों को सिर नवाया। बाद में लैडन ताम्रपट गर्व से लिखता है — अब तोण्डैमंडलम पर उनकी मोहर है।

panels.shot: interior temple shot, Aditya making a grant
panels.action: Inside a temple hall, Aditya stands before priests and officials, extending a copper plate grant toward a Brahmin as sculpted pillars and oil lamps frame the scene.

dialogue.text: From Kanchi and its hinterland, Aditya endowed temples and linked the northern Tamil plain to the Kaveri world. These grants secured loyalty and proclaimed new authority.

i18n.hi: कांची और उसके इर्द–गिर्द से आदित्य ने मंदिर बसाए और उत्तरी तमिल मैदान को कावेरी दुनिया से जोड़ा। इन दानों ने निष्ठा पक्की की और नई सत्ता का ऐलान किया।

panels.shot: transition shot showing generations, Aditya in foreground, faint overlay of Rajaraja and Rajendra as silhouettes
panels.action: Aditya stands in firm profile, while behind him in fainter layers loom the imposing silhouettes of Rajaraja and Rajendra, with a backdrop of ships, forts, and distant lands.

dialogue.text: By taking Tondaimandalam, Aditya gave his descendants a northern base. From this hinge, Rajaraja and Rajendra would later unfurl the Chola empire deep into the seas.

i18n.hi: तोण्डैमंडलम लेकर आदित्य ने वंशजों को उत्तरी गढ़ दिया। इसी कड़ी से राजराज और राजेन्द्र ने बाद में चोल साम्राज्य को समंदरों तक फैला दिया।

panels.shot: close-up of Tiruvalangadu plates under lamplight
panels.action: A hand turns the Tiruvalangadu copper plates under flickering lamplight, the engraved lines catching the glow as a modern scholar’s shadow falls across them.

dialogue.text: The Tiruvalangadu plates, composed long after, praise Aditya’s triumph. Yet they also remind us that we see this turning only through Chola memory, not Pallava lament.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में लिखी तिरुवालंगाडु ताम्रपट आदित्य की जीत का गुणगान करती है। पर साथ ही याद दिलाती है — यह मोड़ हम सिर्फ़ चोल की याद से देखते हैं, पल्लव के दर्द से नहीं।

panels.shot: final wide over Kanchi and the Ariyil landscape at dawn, timeless feel
panels.action: A serene dawn panorama links the towers of Kanchi and the quiet course of the Ariyil river, the land unhurried under soft light, with faint ghostlike impressions of Aparajita and Aditya facing different horizons.

dialogue.text: An ally became a conqueror, and a dynasty fell without a farewell. Their story reminds us: maps change when ambition grows, but the land quietly carries both the victory and the silence.

i18n.hi: दोस्त विजेता बना और एक राजवंश बिना विदाई के ढह गया। उनकी कथा कहती है — जब लालसा बढ़ती है, नक्शे बदलते हैं, पर धरती चुपचाप जीत भी ढोती है और खामोशी भी।
